newsitem.title: USA: Colorado warplane crash site has not yielded bombs.
newsitem.headline: Colorado warplane crash site has not yielded bombs.

text.p: An Air Force team searching for three weeks for wreckage from a warplane that crashed into a Colorado mountain has still not located the four 500-pound bombs that were aboard the plane, officials said Monday.
"I cannot tell you with 100 percent certainty that the bombs are on that mountain until we have them in our hands," Brig. Gen. Don Streater said in a statement.
But Streater said there was no evidence to suggest that the bombs were anywhere other than on Gold Dust Peak, near Vail, Colo.
An A-10 warplane piloted by Capt. Craig Button disappeared mysteriously April 2 during a training mission after taking off from Davis-Monthan Air Force base in Arizona.

By the end of the month, rescue workers had found scraps of metal from the plane and Button's partial remains, but the search operation had to be suspended until warmer weather melted some of the snow on the 13,000-foot mountain.
